description: Keep only the ten Swiss CV templates. For each of them, the Preview shows the pages the PDF and the Word file will have, and the three formats agree page by page.

userStories.title: Only the ten Swiss templates exist
userStories.description: As a user, I want to choose only among the ten Swiss templates, and to find my existing CVs in a Swiss template, so that every CV I make follows the Swiss formats.
acceptanceCriteria: The template picker, everywhere it appears (new CV, CV from a job application, CV from a job offer), offers exactly the ten Swiss templates, in their current order.
A new CV defaults to `swissCommerce` in every creation flow, and the database column default is `swissCommerce`.

A forward migration remaps every stored row: `professional` to `swissTrades`, `modern` to `swissEngineering`, `classic` to `swissFinance`, `minimal` to `swissVocational`, `creative` to `swissFirstJob`. It then narrows `resumes_template_check` to the ten Swiss identifiers. Applied on local Supabase over rows holding each legacy id, it leaves no legacy id and changes no other column. The generated types list the ten identifiers.
The job-application and AI generation routes reject a legacy id (400), as they reject any unknown id.
A stored or drafted template id that is not one of the ten renders as `swissCommerce` in the Editor, Preview, PDF and Word, and never throws.
No production source file, registry entry, locale key or print rule exists only for a legacy resume template. Cover-letter `modern` is untouched.
The tests, visual baselines and parity suite that exist only for legacy templates are removed. Shared-behaviour tests that used a legacy id use a Swiss id instead and still pass.
The `pnpm test:parity` script and the CI `parity` job are removed with the suite. `.claude/rules/resumes.md` names the ten Swiss identifiers as the supported set.

FR-1: The only resume template identifiers are `swissVocational`, `swissCommerce`, `swissTrades`, `swissHealth`, `swissFinance`, `swissEngineering`, `swissIt`, `swissExecutive`, `swissAcademic` and `swissFirstJob`. The default and the unknown-id fallback is `swissCommerce`.
FR-2: The legacy remap is fixed: `professional`→`swissTrades`, `modern`→`swissEngineering`, `classic`→`swissFinance`, `minimal`→`swissVocational`, `creative`→`swissFirstJob`.
FR-3: One geometry per template defines its print page margins. The PDF print CSS, the Preview pagination and the Word generator all read it, and a unit test holds them equal.
FR-4: The Preview's sheets and the PDF's pages contain the same items in the same order. The PDF remains the authority: the e2e compares the Preview with it, not the reverse.
FR-5: Preview pagination never changes the printed output: it is applied only in screen media.
Regression constraint: Page 1 of each template's PDF keeps its current look, except for the foot margin added in US-002.
Regression constraint: Content, section order, hidden items, contact visibility and the photo stay as they are in all three formats.
Regression constraint: The no-word-splitting rule holds in fr, en, de and it.
Regression constraint: Cover letters, their PDF and their Word export are unchanged.
Regression constraint: The PDF route's security behaviour is unchanged: auth, size limits, network policy.

Verification: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm lint` (count compared with the ceiling), plus `pnpm test:visual` on the final diff of each story.
Verification: US-001: migration evidence on local Supabase, with rows of each legacy id before and after, and the constraint and default after.
Verification: US-002 and US-005: the audit fixture's PDF and Word file rendered for each of the ten templates in fr and de, pages compared side by side with the Preview, and the images inspected.
Verification: US-003: rendered browser evidence of the Preview and the Editor live preview at two pages, plus the e2e page-agreement test.
Verification: `ui-expert` validation for US-001, US-002, US-003 and US-005, and `code-reviewer` for every story.

userStories.title: Every printed page has margins, in the PDF and in Word
userStories.description: As a user printing a two-page CV, I want page 2 to start below a top margin and every page to end above a foot margin, so that no text touches the paper's edge.
acceptanceCriteria: For swissVocational, swissCommerce, swissTrades, swissHealth, swissFinance and swissEngineering, the text on every PDF page after the first starts at least 48 px below the paper's top edge.
On every page of those six templates, the last line of text ends at least 48 px above the paper's foot.

Full-bleed backgrounds still reach the paper's edges on every page: the swissCommerce header band on page 1, the swissTrades dark column, the swissEngineering light column and blue bar, and the swissVocational red rule.
Page 1 of the PDF is otherwise unchanged; the existing visual baselines for the six templates still pass, or the diff is limited to the foot margin.
The Word file of each of the six templates uses the same top margin on pages after the first and the same foot margin as the PDF.
The four templates that already had these margins are unchanged.

userStories.title: The Preview shows the real pages
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Preview and the Editor's live preview to show my CV as the separate A4 pages it will print on, with the same items on each page as the PDF, so that I can judge page 2 before exporting.
acceptanceCriteria: The Preview page and the Editor's live preview draw the CV as separate A4 sheets, 794 × 1123 px each, with a visible gap between them. The last sheet is drawn full height.

On screen, an item that print keeps whole moves whole to the next sheet, as it does in print. Such an item is any element the template marks `break-inside-avoid`, and a section heading together with its first item. Every sheet after the first starts its content at the template's print top margin. No line of text is cut by a sheet edge or drawn in a sheet's margin.
Full-bleed backgrounds that print on every page (sidebars and columns) are drawn on every sheet.

For each of the ten templates and the audit fixture, in fr and de, the Preview's sheet count equals the PDF's page count. The first text item of each Preview sheet is the first text item of the same PDF page. This is asserted by an e2e test that runs locally and on the Linux CI.
The pagination is screen-only derived state: the printed PDF is produced by print fragmentation exactly as before, and nothing about it is stored in the resume or its layout model.
It follows edits in the Editor without a reload, and the page-count label and indicators agree with the sheets.

userStories.title: Word keeps every paragraph of an experience
userStories.description: As a user exporting to Word, I want each experience's description paragraph to be kept next to its bullet list, as in the Preview.
acceptanceCriteria: In every Swiss template's Word file, an experience (and an education or project entry, where the template draws one) that has both a description paragraph and a list shows both. They appear in the Preview's order, and no text is lost.
A unit test per affected generator asserts the paragraph's text in `word/document.xml`, and a Word render of the audit fixture shows it.

userStories.title: Word shows the template's typeface and breaks its pages where the PDF does
userStories.description: As a user opening the Word file on any computer, I want it to look like the Preview and to break its pages at the same items as the PDF.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Swiss template's Word file embeds the faces of Inter it uses (as TrueType, obfuscated as Word requires). Word on a computer without Inter installed then renders those runs in Inter, not a substitute. Templates whose fonts are standard system fonts (Georgia, Arial) are unchanged.
In Word, an entry that the template keeps whole in print is kept whole (keep lines together, and keep with next inside the entry). A section heading is kept with its first entry.

For each of the ten templates and the audit fixture, in fr and de, the Word page count equals the PDF page count. The first entry of each Word page is the first entry of the same PDF page, verified on a Microsoft Word render.
The Word file still opens in Word without a repair prompt. Its size grows by no more than the embedded font data.
